summary: Service-broker UI 403 after SSO login due to session cookie path mismatch
description: Issue summary: Several internal users report 403 Forbidden when opening the service-broker UI immediately after completing Okta SSO. The main Redwood console and most services authenticate fine; the service-broker UI (path /services/broker) is the only product page consistently returning 403 after a successful Okta redirect. Impact: ~12 engineers reported inability to access service-broker workflows; blocks a small number of oncall tasks that require approving dedicated capacity requests. Environment: prod us-east, observed from browser sessions on Chrome and Firefox. Steps to reproduce: 1) Sign in via Okta SSO to console.redwood.ai 2) Click the Services -> Broker entry (navigates to console.redwood.ai/services/broker) 3) Observe redirect to /auth/callback then immediate 403 on /services/broker Expected behavior: SSO redirect results in an authenticated session and the browser should include the Okta session cookie so the /services/broker route allows access. Actual behavior: The browser receives Set-Cookie on auth callback with Path=/console but requests to /services/broker do not include that cookie, resulting in a 403 from the backend. Temporary observations: - Network tab shows Set-Cookie: Redwood-SSO=...; Path=/console; Secure; HttpOnly - Subsequent GET to /services/broker does not include Redwood-SSO header. - Other console paths under /console/ include cookie and work normally. - This started after last ingress gateway deployment on 2026-03-08. Logs: - proxy logs show cookie rewrite for paths outside /console - backend reports 401->403 mapping when session missing Additional context: Several users used Incognito and cleared cookies with same result. Issue appears to be an ingress-side regression that changed cookie path or rewrote path attribute for SSO sessions.
investigation_notes: - 2026-03-10 10:15: Reviewed network traces from affected user (user: amanda.liu@redwood). Confirmed Set-Cookie Path=/console. - 2026-03-10 11:05 Pulled ingress-gateway helm chart diff vs previous: found new annotation ingress.kubernetes.io/cookie-path: /console added in 2026-03-08 deploy. - 2026-03-10 13:30 Reproduced locally by toggling cookie-path annotation: when cookie-path=/console access to /services/* fails. - Hypothesis: ingress-gateway change scoped Okta session cookie to /console only; service-broker lives at /services so cookie not sent. - Cross-checked with auth-service: session validation expects Redwood-SSO cookie present on all console subpaths; currently validation middleware checks cookie regardless of request path which means scoping cookie to /console prevents access to /services endpoints. - Noted linked request INT-11205 had a concurrent SCIM/role propagation change but unrelated to cookie behavior. - Captured proxy config and exported for GH PR 447 which contains proposed fix to remove cookie-path scoping and restore path=/.
comments: Support (2026-03-10) - Jonah Kim: Initial triage done; reproduced in staging with cookie-path annotation present. Marking P1 due to oncall impact.
SRE (2026-03-10) - Maria Torres: Ingress change in rollout on 2026-03-08 added cookie-path annotation during a refactor (PR 432). Rolling back that annotation in a canary should validate hypothesis.

Eng (2026-03-11) - Priya Singh: Created github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-gateway/pull/447 to remove the annotation and consolidate cookie scoping logic. Running integration tests against staging now.
Support (2026-03-12) - Jonah Kim: Customers on Dedicated reported no impact; this is internal-only because service-broker is internal path. Keep internal comms updated in #internal-support.

SRE (2026-03-12) - Maria Torres: Canary rollback applied to cluster staging-us-east-1. Verified that Set-Cookie now uses Path=/ and /services/broker accepts authenticated requests in the canary. Scheduling prod rollback pending approvals.
resolution: Workaround: Engineers can access the service-broker UI by using the console entrypoint under /console/services/broker or by logging in and manually setting the cookie scope via developer tools (temporary and not recommended). Permanent fix: Revert ingress annotation that scoped the session cookie to /console and update integration tests to assert cookie path = /. A PR with the change (ingress-gateway PR 447) is open; plan is to deploy rollback to prod during low-traffic window and then follow with a forward-compatible change that centralizes cookie scoping logic in auth-service. Post-deploy verification steps documented in related_confluence_pages.
